cells: STUDENT IA PLANNING DOCUMENT  |  Proposed output specification

The personalised summary includes student choices, alternatives, predictions, data-method rationale, full milestones, proposed first representation, potential adjustments and teacher questions. Available from every route.
PDF default, optional editable Word. Report length adapts to the student's answers; avoid padding a fixed IA-writing template or including irrelevant content.
Student reviews answers before exporting. Optional unanswered planning prompts remain 'To be confirmed' rather than blocking output or receiving an automatic low score.
Pending teacher discussion changes the report STATUS, never export access. For restricted data, do not collect/use affected information before required approval.
This tab is the DOCUMENT DESIGN SPECIFICATION. No student-facing document generator has been implemented.
How it appears in final document
Working IA title or aim; course (AI SL / AA SL); optional student identifier; generation date
'My IB Mathematics IA Plan' with clearly labelled draft status and date
All; identifier optional, no unnecessary personal details
A short heading; not the final IA title or formal cover sheet.
Investigation aim, personal benefit and intended audience

Student's aim, motivation, current chosen beneficiary (self, another audience, or both), what the investigation could help them decide/understand, and why it matters. Include any edits made during prediction.
Use the most recently confirmed 'Who is it for?' answer; do not retain outdated audience text if the student has changed it during prediction.
Every planning route, including teacher-led ideas; uncertainty never prevents a summary.
State the *intended* possible use, not a guaranteed or evidence-proven outcome. Do not generate the student's introduction.
Primary / secondary / both; exactly what is measured; variable(s) and units
A simple source-and-variables summary; direct hyperlink for secondary dataset
Only for primary, secondary or both. A no-data route records the idea in the teacher section, not fabricated data fields.
Reference original secondary data, not a pasted full dataset.
When, where, who/what, how, measurement tools/equipment and relevant survey design
Compact collection checklist and student-provided answers
Only if Primary or Both chosen
Add the choice of an alternative data-collection method and why the actual method was selected, including acceptable limitations (N03J).
Exact source URL, publisher, relevant fields/columns, intended subset and verification status
Clickable source URL and short description; student-selected columns
Only if Secondary or Both chosen
Only include the relevant secondary-data columns, source reference and justification; do not dump entire dataset into the report.
First usable data target; full dataset target; proposed collection/start date
Two labelled dates and a short note on starting mathematical work
Data-based routes only. For no-data/theoretical route, omit dates or label them 'Not applicable'.
Maintain the distinction between first usable data and complete collection; longer draft and revision milestones are in the full timeline (N03H).
Calculated/provisional score, evidence, reason, one suggested improvement
For data-based IAs: score /5 plus reasons. No-data: 'Not applicable — discuss with teacher'. Unclear evidence: 'Not yet assessed'.
Show score only when data readiness applies; N/A and unassessed do not equal 0/5.
5/5 requires usable data; 4/5 can reflect a convincing near-term plan.
Rating, dependencies, permissions/access, tool/software burden, workload, fallback
Show a completion-ease score only where enough practical details have been supplied. Otherwise display 'Not yet assessed' and state what remains unresolved.
Any route with sufficient practical information; otherwise explain why the rating is pending.
Separate from data readiness; unresolved safety/consent flags cannot be hidden by a high score.
Possible combined score or summary status; scoring approach not yet approved
Show a clearly labelled placeholder or omit until agreed
Only once overall plan rating system is agreed
Never average a 'Not applicable' or 'Not yet assessed' element as 0. Overall plan rating remains to be agreed.
Initial course-maths selections; student-selected additions/removals after prediction; any outside-course technique; why methods may fit the expected data.
Show proposed mathematics as provisional, explicitly distinguishing the student's choices from website suggestions.
Any route. No-data and other-course students can use optional free-text maths instead of a course-specific menu.
Outside-course mathematics should trigger teacher discussion, not automatic rejection.
If suitability cannot be judged, show 'Teacher review needed' and the student's proposed method, not an automatic failure.
All routes, including no-data, AA HL, outside-course or uncertain mathematics.
Use the prediction plus the planned data type and sample structure when considering suitability; do not assume prediction is correct.
Data delays, practical obstacles, method/sampling limitations, timetable bottlenecks and uncertainty, but only the few most consequential for this plan.
Only the 2–3 most significant risks, each linked to a possible mitigation
Only when a real risk or uncertainty is identified
Never paste every generic warning into the report; flag consent and safeguarding separately.
Student's first meaningful maths action and the planned graph/table/diagram or simplified example that will help start the investigation.
A specific safe mathematical first step if supplied; otherwise 'To discuss with teacher'.
All routes. Optional if teacher questions remain; never instruct unsafe or restricted collection.
Do not automatically write a mathematical method or analysis on the student's behalf.
Date for first representation, initial calculation, writing a complete teacher draft, checking and corrections, known school deadlines, and one next action.
Short prioritised action list with dates if known
All routes, including provisional plans awaiting teacher feedback.
Proposed recommendations must be clearly distinguished from student-supplied commitments.
Optional teacher question offered to every student (N06T) plus any targeted teacher-check-in notes (N08), including no-data or permission issues.
Clearly labelled 'To discuss with my teacher' section with the student's own short answers and unresolved decisions.
All routes may record a question; specialist flags are conspicuous but should not prevent export.
Never imply the teacher has approved a topic just because a report was generated.
Footer: 'Planning aid, not an IB assessment or guaranteed topic approval'
Planning report is a snapshot. It may be revised as an investigation unfolds; it is not a rigid IA writing structure or teacher approval.
Consultation trigger(s), question(s) for the teacher, plan fields still unknown, next safe step and relevant student explanation.
When flagged, headline says 'Provisional plan — teacher discussion needed'. Unanswered nonessential fields say 'To be confirmed'.
Only teacher-advice routes; summary still available before feedback.
When approval remains outstanding, the report flags it; all students can record a universal teacher question even without a specialist flag.
Up to two alternatives, quick feasibility comparison and the student's reason for the chosen provisional idea.
Concise comparison note only if entered; one idea does not earn a lower rating.
Only when student uses optional comparison.
Avoid a separate detailed plan/score for each candidate topic.

Student's chosen prediction (or Not sure yet); WHY they expect it; IF TRUE what it could mean for the intended beneficiary; any uncertainty; and revised mathematical techniques kept separate as student selections.
Two distinct student statements: 'Why I expect this' and 'What it might mean for [beneficiary] if true'. Explicitly hypothetical; don't make recommendations on untested data.
Show only questions answered; 'Not sure yet' is acceptable.
Retain the student's own conditional implication; if 'Who is it for?' was edited, use current beneficiary fields. This is not a demonstrated finding, promise or predicted grade.
Choice of data method and limitations
Alternative data source or sampling method, reason for selection, main limitation and any mitigation.
One clear rationale and important limitation rather than a long generic methods essay.
Data-based plans, conditionally detailed for surveys.
Known school deadlines, first representation, initial mathematics, complete draft, feedback, revisions and contingency buffer.
Compact project-specific milestone table, with editable dates and 'To confirm' for unknown school deadlines.
All routes; no invented deadlines or false date-based scoring.
Warnings for impossible sequences or no time to act on feedback.
Which graph, table, sketch or simplified model student intends to make and why it is useful.
One-line description, not a mandatory finished graph.
Belongs to planning: full diagram presentation remains in Completing the IA.

Possible changes of direction after an unexpected result or practical obstacle (especially unavailable data): alternative approved collection, credible secondary source, narrower scope, or method/aim adjustment with a reason.
Short 'If this happens, I could...' note where offered.
Keep the original aim, prediction and intended beneficiary visible. Planning can be progressed before data arrive; Completing offers short, optional C95D/C95A support.
Optional question for the teacher and intended discussion date alongside any mandatory specialist flags.
'Questions I could discuss with my teacher' plus required review warning where applicable.
Available to every student; never an export blocker.
Suggested conversation for all; specific permissions needed before affected actions.
Stable field IDs and a schema version; answers, selected maths, prediction/why, risks and permission flags, milestones and original report date.
Readable PDF/DOCX with embedded versioned resume data plus labelled field text to help recovery; never the IA itself.
All planning exports, including provisional teacher-review cases.
Reuploading the Pathfinder PDF or Word prepopulates editable fields. If import fails, allow partial recovery or manual entry. A JSON backup is optional, not mandatory.
